sentences.text: The prosecution allegation is that, the petitioners, who are the husband and in-laws of the 2nd respondent/de- facto complainant, subjected her to matrimonial cruelties, demanding more gold ornaments and money.

3. When the matter is taken up for consideration, learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that, the matter has been amicably settled and he produced Annexure- III, affidavit filed by CRL.MC NO. 756 OF 2024 2025:KER:9724 the de-facto complainant, stating that the entire dispute has been settled, and she is not intending to prosecute this matter any further.

4. Learned Public Prosecutor obtained instructions regarding the settlement, and he produced signed statement of the de-facto complainant's mother, on behalf of her daughter, in which she has stated that, she has no objection in quashing Annexure-1 final report and the proceedings pursuant thereto.

An affidavit sworn by the de facto complainant attested by the Consulate General of India,
Birmingham (U.K.) also is produced which says that all the disputes between the de facto complainant and the petitioners herein are settled, and she has no objection in quashing all further proceedings as against the petitioners in the above-said case.

Since the dispute is purely personal in nature, and no public interest is involved in it, this Court is of the view that, there is no purpose in Steny Selvaraj vs State Of Kerala on 4 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3576220/
2 proceeding with the criminal prosecution initiated against the petitioners.
